football_evidence.question: Can South Florida’s pass rush get to Ryder Burton?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward South Florida, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.5 of the 5.9 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When UAB has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): UAB’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.9% of its dropbacks, and South Florida’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When UAB has the ball (the red zone): UAB’s offense succeeds on 33.4% of its red-zone plays, and South Florida’s defense allows success on 34.2% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When UAB has the ball (big plays through the air): UAB’s offense turns 7.5% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and South Florida’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When UAB has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): UAB’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 17.6% of its runs, and South Florida’s defense stops 22.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
contradicting: When South Florida has the ball (big plays on the ground): South Florida’s offense turns 4.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and UAB’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
